Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Housing Authority on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Housing Authority, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Sergeant at Arms. The Housing Authority will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and
prior to a vote. The Housing Authority will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications
period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency
or special circumstances exist. The Housing Authority may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration
at a future Housing Authority meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Housing Authority:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Housing Authority as a whole and not directed to individual Commissioners.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s office, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Housing Authority regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular
business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720.
You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

   ATTACHMENT 1
  Housing Authority
  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Kristin Maithonis at ext. 5653 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT: INTERAGENCY AGREEMENT WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY FOR PROJECT-BASED VETERANS
  AFFAIRS SUPPORTIVE HOUSING VOUCHERS FOR MERCY HOUSING
  CALIFORNIA DEVELOPMENT

Background:

Mercy Housing California (Mercy Housing) is proposing to develop sixty (60) rental
housing units affordable to low-income veterans and their families on a City owned
property on the corner of Foster Road and San Antonio Drive. Mercy Housing has filed
an application with the City and is currently seeking planning approvals. The
development is to include twenty (20) supportive housing units (units for veterans
confronted with homelessness and who also have very low incomes and/or serious
persistent health or psychological issues). The provision of these units at an affordable
rent necessitates project-based (PB) Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH)
vouchers.

Since the Norwalk Housing Authority (Authority) does not have a VASH program, Mercy
Housing is requesting VASH vouchers from the Los Angeles County Development
Authority (LACDA). Per Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) program description,
“the VASH program combines Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance for homeless
veterans and their families with case management and clinical services provided by the
Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).” Because the development is located in the
Authority’s jurisdiction, LACDA is requesting an interagency agreement with the Authority.

Under the agreement, LACDA would administer and fund the PB VASH vouchers at the
Mercy Housing development. The Authority would have no financial or administrative
obligations under the VASH program. The term of the agreement would end on the same
date of the PB VASH Contract between LACDA and Mercy Housing.
 Housing Authority  November 19, 2019
Interagency Agreement for PB VASH  Page No. 2

On May 16, 2017, LACDA and the Authority entered into an interagency agreement
allowing LACDA to administer PB vouchers at Birch Grove Homes and Elm Street Homes
located on the grounds of the Metropolitan State Hospital. The arrangement has been
working well.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation: N/A

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority approve an interagency agreement with the
Los Angeles County Development Authority to allow for project-based Veterans Affairs
Supportive Housing Vouchers for the Mercy Housing development; and authorize the
Executive Director to execute the interagency agreement, on behalf of the Housing
Authority, in a form approved by the Authority Counsel.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION NO. NHA-160 - AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF AN
  APPLICATION TO THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING
  AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT FOR THE TENANT PROTECTION
  VOUCHERS FOR FOSTER YOUTH TO INDEPENDENCE INITIATIVE
  AND AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR TO EXECUTE ANY
  REQUIRED AGREEMENTS

Background:

The Housing Authority (Authority) currently administers 705 Housing Choice Vouchers
for very low-income households through funding provided by the United States
Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The program delivers rental
assistance to help eligible, very low-income residents afford to rent units in the private
market.

On July 26, 2019, HUD announced the availability of funds under a special program
targeted to foster youth between the ages of 18 and 24 who are homeless or at risk of
homelessness. The purpose of the vouchers is to facilitate partnerships to end
homelessness, which is one of the stated goals of “Home Together: The Federal Strategic
Plan to Prevent and End Homelessness.” To be eligible for the Foster Youth to
Independence Tenant Protection Vouchers (FYI TPV), the Authority must partner with the
Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS). Under the program, DCFS is
responsible for referring homeless and at risk foster youth to the Authority and providing
on-going case management to participants.

The vouchers are time-limited and sunset after three years. After a voucher is terminated
or sunsets, it cannot be re-issued to another foster youth. The program provides funding
for the Housing Assistance Payment and administrative costs for up to 25 vouchers.
Applications for these special vouchers are being accepted on a rolling basis until funding
 Housing Authority  November 19, 2019
Resolution No. NHA-160 – Foster Youth to Independence  Page No. 2

is exhausted. It is anticipated that new FYI TPVs will be offered by HUD annually for the
next several years.

In order to apply, the Authority must have an executed Memorandum of Understanding
(MOU) with DCFS and a list of eligible foster youth referred by DCFS. DCFS is eager to
partner with the Authority and enter into a MOU. Because the youth must be identified in
the request for funding, the Authority is able to request the vouchers in multiple batches
of as little as one (1) at a time until a total of 25 vouchers have been requested. An
amendment to the Section 8 Administrative Plan will be needed to add a new special
purpose voucher preference and termination provisions. If this item is approved, staff will
return with recommended amendments to the Administrative Plan at a future meeting.

At this time, vacant apartments are scarce, and voucher holders are having difficulty
finding housing in Norwalk despite numerous landlord incentives being offered. Because
of the lack of available housing, vouchers are going unused or participants are leaving
the City in search of housing elsewhere. If a FYI TPV participant is unsuccessful in
securing housing or transfers to another housing authority and that housing authority
absorbs the participant into their program, the FYI TPV will sunset and cannot be reissued
to another eligible foster youth.

In an effort to retain the FYI TPVs and increase housing options, staff recommends
entering into an Interagency Agreement with the Los Angeles County Development
Authority (LACDA). The Interagency Agreement would allow the Authority to continue to
administer FYI TPV participants who locate housing in the surrounding unincorporated
areas and cities of La Mirada, Whittier, Santa Fe Springs, Downey, and Bellflower. If a
participant finds housing in areas of the County far from Norwalk, where staff limitations
would prohibit continued administration of the voucher, the Authority would transfer the
voucher to LACDA.

Applying for additional rental vouchers is one of the goals contained in the Housing
Authority’s adopted 5-Year Public Housing Agency Plan. Additional vouchers targeting
foster youth who are homeless and at risk of homelessness will support the City’s effort
in preventing and combatting homelessness.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised: N/A

Strategic Action Plan Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s strategic plan goal of: (2.A.1) Actively
seeking and applying for grants to support City programs and projects.
 Housing Authority  November 19, 2019
Resolution No. NHA-160 – Foster Youth to Independence  Page No. 3

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Housing Authority:

a. adopt RESOLUTION NO. NHA-160, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  HOUSING AUTHORITY AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF AN APPLICATION TO THE
  UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT
  FOR THE TENANT PROTECTION VOUCHERS FOR FOSTER YOUTH TO
  INDEPENDENCE INITIATIVE AND AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
  TO EXECUTE ANY REQUIRED AGREEMENTS;

b. approve a Memorandum of Understanding with the Department of Children and
  Family Services to provide referral and supportive services; and authorize the
  Executive Director to execute the Memorandum of Understanding and any
  amendments, on behalf of the Housing Authority, in a form approved by the Authority
  Counsel; and

c. approve an Interagency Agreement with the Los Angeles County Development
  Authority to allow for administration of Foster Youth to Independence Initiative Tenant
  Protection Vouchers inside the Los Angeles County Development Authority’s
  jurisdiction; and authorize the Executive Director to execute the Interagency
  Agreement, on behalf of the Housing Authority, in a form approved by the Authority
  Counsel.

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
  AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF AN APPLICATION TO THE UNITED

  WHEREAS, funds are being made available under the United States Department
of Housing and Urban Development Notice PIH 2019-20 for the Tenant Protection
Vouchers for Foster Youth to Independence Initiative;

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk Housing Authority, being established in
accordance with Section 34290 et.seq., of the California Health and Safety Code, is
administering the Housing Choice Voucher Program and is eligible to apply under the
Notice;

  WHEREAS, applying for additional rental vouchers is a goal contained within City
of Norwalk Housing Authority’s Five-Year Public Housing Agency Plan for 2015-2020
adopted on February 17, 2015;

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk Housing Authority has determined that there is a
need for vouchers targeted to foster youth who are homeless or at risk of homelessness;
and

  WHEREAS, if funding is awarded under the Tenant Protection Vouchers for Foster
Youth to Independence Initiative, the City of Norwalk Housing Authority will amend the
Administrative Plan waiting list preferences and termination provisions to align with the
program requirements.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE CITY OF NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY
HEREBY DETERMINES, FINDS, AND RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. That the Executive Director or his designee is authorized to execute
and submit the application, documentation and any required grant or funding award
agreements for Foster Youth to Independence Initiative Tenant Protection Vouchers.

  Section 2. That the Executive Director is authorized to execute a Memorandum
of Understanding with the Department of Children and Family Services to provide referral
and supportive services for the Foster Youth to Independence Initiative Tenant Protection
Vouchers.

  Section 3. That the Executive Director is authorized to execute an Interagency
Agreement with the Los Angeles County Development Authority allowing for
 administration of Foster Youth to Independence Initiative Tenant Protection Vouchers
inside the Los Angeles County Development Authority’s jurisdiction.

  APPROVED AND ADOPTED on this 19th day of November 2019.
